paragraphs.source_en: At Genkei's house near Kōzanji Temple, summer cicadas filled the air with their cries. The leaves beyond the grounds stirred gently, yet no breeze entered, and the courtyard was stiflingly hot.

units.source_zh: 我看看。”

paragraphs.source_en: Genkei had only one servant, and the old woman happened to be out that day.

units.source_en: Genkei had only one servant, and the old woman happened to be out that day.

units.source_zh: “玄黄。”

paragraphs.source_en: “No.” The other man shook his head. “He is still on his sickbed. Farewell.” The bamboo-tube seller quietly left Genkei’s house and went on his way, crying his wares.

paragraphs.source_en: Somewhat puzzled, Genkei returned to his bedchamber. Two secret letters had arrived: one for him and the other for Lady Tsukiyama. Genkei rose cautiously, coughed dryly as he peered into the corridor, then swiftly opened the envelope. At Katsuyori’s command, Genkei had sent Lady Tsukiyama’s letter to Kai, and only now had a reply come.

units.source_en: Somewhat puzzled, Genkei returned to his bedchamber.
units.source_zh: 减敬有些不解地回到卧房。

paragraphs.source_zh: 减敬有些不解地回到卧房。送过来两封密函，一封给他，另一封给筑山夫人。减敬警惕地站起来，干咳着望了望走廊，然后飞快打开信封。接到胜赖的命令，减敬将筑山夫人的信送到了甲斐，现在才有回音。

paragraphs.source_en: Lady Tsukiyama’s letter remained clearly engraved in Genkei’s memory—

units.source_en: Lady Tsukiyama’s letter remained clearly engraved in Genkei’s memory—
units.source_zh: 筑山夫人的那封信，至今仍然清楚地刻在减敬的脑中——

paragraphs.source_zh: 筑山夫人的那封信，至今仍然清楚地刻在减敬的脑中——

paragraphs.source_en: Nobuyasu is my son and will surely be able to serve the Takeda clan. In the coming struggle, the Tokugawa and Oda houses are certain to be defeated. When the affair is accomplished, I ask that the former Tokugawa domains be bestowed upon my son Nobuyasu. I also hope that a husband of suitable rank may be found for me. If these wishes can be granted, I beg you to send a reply.

units.source_en: Nobuyasu is my son and will surely be able to serve the Takeda clan.
units.source_zh: > 信康乃我儿，定能为武田氏效力。

units.source_en: In the coming struggle, the Tokugawa and Oda houses are certain to be defeated.
units.source_zh: 此次德川、织田两家必败。

units.source_en: When the affair is accomplished, I ask that the former Tokugawa domains be bestowed upon my son Nobuyasu.

units.source_en: I also hope that a husband of suitable rank may be found for me.

units.source_en: If these wishes can be granted, I beg you to send a reply.

paragraphs.source_en: “Whatever happens, we must win this war.” Muttering to himself, Genkei opened the secret letter written in Katsuyori’s own hand. In it, Katsuyori gave him permission to read the letter addressed to Lady Tsukiyama.

units.source_en: “Whatever happens, we must win this war.”
units.source_zh: “无论如何，必须赢得这场战争。”

paragraphs.source_en: I am greatly relieved to learn through Genkei that you are in good health.

units.source_en: I am greatly relieved to learn through Genkei that you are in good health.
units.source_zh: > 经由减敬获悉贵体安好，甚慰。

paragraphs.source_zh: > 经由减敬获悉贵体安好，甚慰。

paragraphs.source_en: I earnestly hope that your son will devote himself to Katsuyori, so that together we may devise the great undertaking of destroying Ieyasu and Nobunaga. Once it is accomplished, not only the former Tokugawa domains but even Nobunaga’s lands may be handed over in their entirety to Saburō, making him lord of a province.

units.source_en: I earnestly hope that your son will devote himself to Katsuyori, so that together we may devise the great undertaking of destroying Ieyasu and Nobunaga.

paragraphs.source_en: As for your request, it happens that one of our domain’s great commanders, Oyamada Hyōe, lost his wife last year; I hope you will consent to marry him. I eagerly await Nobuyasu and the other gentlemen escorting Lady Tsukiyama into Kai and Shinano, where we may celebrate the occasion.

units.source_en: As for your request, it happens that one of our domain’s great commanders, Oyamada Hyōe, lost his wife last year; I hope you will consent to marry him.

paragraphs.source_en: Genkei stole a glance around him, hurriedly rolled up the letter, and struck a flint. He meant first to burn the letter Katsuyori had written to him. As he watched the secret letter crumble into white ash and drift down, Genkei broke out in a cold sweat.

paragraphs.source_en: The secret pact between Lady Tsukiyama and Katsuyori was now settled. Katsuyori had readily granted Lady Tsukiyama’s demand that the former Tokugawa domains be retained, and had even promised to give Nobuyasu part of Nobunaga’s territory. Oyamada Hyōe’s standing in Kai was lofty enough to set the heart of Lady Tsukiyama—who could no longer endure the loneliness of her bedchamber—aflutter.

units.source_en: The secret pact between Lady Tsukiyama and Katsuyori was now settled.
units.source_zh: 筑山夫人和胜赖之间的密约已定。

units.source_en: Katsuyori had readily granted Lady Tsukiyama’s demand that the former Tokugawa domains be retained, and had even promised to give Nobuyasu part of Nobunaga’s territory.

paragraphs.source_en: The enemy was not outside the castle, but within it. Ieyasu knew nothing of it and had left Okazaki early to recover Suruga from the Yamaga Sanpō faction. Thinking of this, Genkei felt that Ieyasu was tragedy embodied. He deliberately went into the courtyard and ground the ashes to dust, then hurriedly made ready to visit Lady Tsukiyama.

paragraphs.source_en: It was not far from his house to the castle. At the thought of the secret letter inside his robe, Genkei’s heart trembled again and again. units.source_en: “How is Her Ladyship?”
units.source_zh: “夫人情况如何？”

units.source_en: “She has just finished dressing her hair and is waiting for you.”

paragraphs.source_en: Startled, Genkei glanced at the koto maid. “It has suddenly grown so hot. If only we could have some rain.” He hurriedly signaled Lady Tsukiyama with his eyes as he changed the subject.

units.source_en: Startled, Genkei glanced at the koto maid.

paragraphs.source_en: Genkei stepped forward in a daze. Why was her ladyship’s skin as cold as a snake, while her breath remained so burning hot? Only recently had Genkei come to understand how terrifying human desire could be. Was a woman’s life nothing more than bearing and raising children? Once a woman reached Lady Tsukiyama’s age, with the bloom of youth about to fade, desire began to run mad—so mad as to verge on the pitiful.
